clue.text: Taxi left — rush back for other transport

parts.note: a taxi is a cab

indicators.note: back tells us the word for rush is read from its end to its start

parts.note: to rush is to race

explanation.surface: A passenger abandons a taxi and hurries off in search of some other way to travel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rush back' could suggest a hurried return journey; 'back' only turns the word for rush.
explanation.definitionFit: A cable car is a vehicle hauled along a wire, a mode of travel different from a taxi.

clue.text: On-screen flasher who swears out loud

indicators.note: out loud means the word is heard spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a person who swears is a curser

explanation.surface: An exhibitionist on television who uses foul language aloud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flasher' suggests an exhibitionist but means the blinking marker on a computer screen.
explanation.definitionFit: The cursor is the blinking marker on a computer display showing where text goes.

clue.text: Lawyer's underpants

explanation.surface: The underwear belonging to a lawyer.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief is slang for a barrister, so 'lawyer's' is brief's; briefs are short close-fitting knickers.

clue.text: In conclusion, am off improving

indicators.note: off shows that the word am is taken away from the longer word

parts.note: improving is amending, as one amends a text
taken as written

explanation.surface: To sum up, I am leaving and getting better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' removes AM from AMENDING. 'In conclusion' looks like a summary but 'conclusion' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An ending is the final part, a close or finish.

clue.text: Higher-up committee is open and honest

parts.note: higher up is above
a board is a governing committee

explanation.surface: A senior committee is said to be transparent and upright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Higher-up' looks like a noun for a boss, but here means above.
explanation.definitionFit: Above board describes dealings that are legitimate, done openly and without deceit.

clue.text: Sad time for unhappy Craig

indicators.note: unhappy suggests the name Craig is disturbed and its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A gloomy spell for a man named Craig who is feeling low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sad' and 'unhappy' both look like definitions; 'unhappy' is the anagram signal working on Craig.
explanation.definitionFit: Tragic and sad are near-synonyms, both describing grievous, sorrowful events.

clue.text: Bypass turbulent Rio Grand

indicators.note: turbulent waters churn, so the letters of Rio Grand are stirred up

explanation.surface: Avoid the stormy waters of the Rio Grande river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rio Grande is a river, missing its final E; 'turbulent' signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring road circles a town so traffic can avoid its centre, like a bypass.

clue.text: Beat back everybody after bishop hit with wood, perhaps

indicators.note: after places the word for everybody behind the bishop's letter
back means the word for beat is turned round

parts.note: to beat is to flog
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
everybody is all

explanation.surface: Everyone fights back after a bishop is struck with a wooden stick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns FLOG into GOLF. A wood is a type of golf club, hence 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: A golf ball is struck with clubs, one kind of which is called a wood.

clue.text: Arrange in categories if in elegant surroundings

indicators.note: surroundings means the word for elegant goes around the little word

parts.note: elegant means classy

explanation.surface: Sorting things into groups, providing the setting is a stylish one.
explanation.definitionFit: To classify is to sort things into groups or classes.

clue.text: Fall from on high in porn raid storm

indicators.note: storm suggests the letters of porn raid are tossed about violently into a new order

explanation.surface: Police storm premises in a raid on pornographers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'storm' looks like the police action but is the anagram signal on PORN RAID.
explanation.definitionFit: Each droplet of rain is something that falls from the clouds above.

clue.text: Ford's England?

explanation.surface: A question about what the car maker Ford regards as its homeland.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ford Anglia was a popular British family car; Anglia is also the Latin name for England, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Ford sold a saloon model under this name; in Latin it is the land of the Angles, England.

clue.text: Wrongdoer to propose to embrace death

indicators.note: to embrace means one word wraps its arms around the other, holding it inside

parts.note: to propose is to offer
death is one's end

explanation.surface: A villain about to make a proposal that involves embracing death.
explanation.definitionFit: An offender is someone who commits a crime or misdeed, a culprit.

clue.text: Attempts to involve British clans

indicators.note: to involve here means to take in, so one word is placed within the other

parts.note: attempts are tries

explanation.surface: Efforts are made to bring British clans into some joint venture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to involve' places B inside TRIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Tribes and clans are both kinship groups claiming a common ancestry.

clue.text: Serving to warn Iran, "You act recklessly"

indicators.note: recklessly suggests the letters are thrown about carelessly into a new order

explanation.surface: A warning to Iran not to behave rashly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recklessly' signals an anagram of IRAN YOU ACT.
explanation.definitionFit: A cautionary tale is one meant as a warning.

clue.text: Novel return for inner restraint

indicators.note: inner says the restraint goes inside the other piece
return asks for the little word that follows to be turned back on itself

parts.note: taken as written
a manacle is a restraint, a shackle for the wrist

explanation.surface: Some new device for returning a restraint that sits on the inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like an adjective meaning new, but names a kind of book; 'inner restraint' reads as self-control.
explanation.definitionFit: A roman a clef is a work of fiction in which real people appear under invented names.

clue.text: Constant, active and frenzied combat in tunnel

parts.note: C is the symbol used for a constant, as for the speed of light
A is a grammatical abbreviation for active

indicators.note: frenzied suggests wild disorder, so the letters of combat are mixed up

explanation.surface: Persistent, energetic and frantic fighting takes place underground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tunnel' is fair: catacombs are networks of underground passages.
explanation.definitionFit: A catacomb is an underground cemetery of passages and chambers.

clue.text: Blunt lie exposed in report

indicators.note: exposed suggests the lie is opened up and its letters laid out differently

explanation.surface: A news report reveals a flat untruth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exposed' signals an anagram of BLUNT LIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A bulletin is a short official statement or news report.

clue.text: Looking fixedly, catches lake bird

indicators.note: catches means the word for looking fixedly takes the lake letter inside it

parts.note: looking fixedly is staring
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: Gazing intently, someone spots a bird beside a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catches' puts L inside STARING.
explanation.definitionFit: The starling is a common speckled songbird.

clue.text: Debase heartless Ted, laureate, in rewrite

indicators.note: rewrite asks for the letters to be written out again in a different order
heartless removes the middle letter of Ted, keeping only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Ted Hughes, poet laureate, is made to look bad by a heartless rewrite of his work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' reduces TED to TD; 'rewrite' rearranges TD with LAUREATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To adulterate is to spoil purity by adding inferior matter, lowering quality.

clue.text: Realise potential if put up in perfect surroundings

indicators.note: surroundings means the word for perfect goes round the other piece

parts.note: perfect in the sense of complete is full

indicators.note: put up in a down clue means the word if is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Achieving one's promise, if placed in an ideal setting.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'put up' means read from bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: To fulfil is to bring to completion, as in achieving one's promise.

clue.text: Monotony is universal in timed broadcast

indicators.note: in places the letter for universal inside the rearranged word
broadcast means scattered, so the letters of timed are spread into a new order

parts.note: U is the film-rating abbreviation for universal

explanation.surface: Dullness is found everywhere in a carefully timed radio show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges TIMED to TEDIM; 'in' puts U inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Tedium is the boredom of something dull and repetitive.

clue.text: Scattered all four points around the room initially

indicators.note: around means the compass letters enclose the other letters

parts.note: the four compass points are S, E, W and N

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: Things are spread all over the room, to every corner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all four points' means the four compass directions, here in the order South, East, West, North.
explanation.definitionFit: Strewn means spread untidily over an area, as things thrown about.

clue.text: A left hook can be seductive

parts.note: a hook or bait is a lure

explanation.surface: A boxer's left hook can be strangely attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hook' suggests boxing but here means bait, a lure.
explanation.definitionFit: To allure is to attract or entice, which is what something seductive does.

clue.text: Paper record

explanation.surface: A paper record.
explanation.definitionFit: A document is an official paper; to document is to record something in writing.

clue.text: Get all at sea in boat

indicators.note: all at sea means confused and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Getting hold of something while one is out on the water in a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all at sea' fits the boat picture but signals an anagram of IN BOAT.
explanation.definitionFit: To obtain something is to acquire it, a synonym for getting.

clue.text: Produced by unusually fine cafe

indicators.note: unusually shows the letters of fine cafe come in an odd, rearranged order

explanation.surface: Something a particularly good coffee shop gives you.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a good cafe produces coffee full of the stimulant, made by rearranging FINE CAFE.
explanation.definitionFit: The stimulant alkaloid in coffee is extracted when a cafe brews its drinks.

clue.text: Comprise less than ten reports, being favourable

indicators.note: reports indicates the words are heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: to comprise is to be or constitute; nine is one less than ten

explanation.surface: Being made of under ten reports counts in the writer's favour.
explanation.walkthrough: BE and NINE spoken together sound like the answer, whose second syllable rhymes with 'nine'.
explanation.definitionFit: Benign means kindly or auspicious, a good sign, hence favourable.

clue.text: Cancel my order for houseplant

indicators.note: order means the letters of cancel my are put into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A homeowner cancels an order placed for a pot plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' reads as a purchase but signals an anagram of CANCEL MY.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyclamen is a flowering plant often grown indoors in pots.
